steps.scene: You're approaching a junction. The lights ahead change from red to red and amber showing together.

question.prompt: What does red and amber together mean?

options.text: Go — that combination means the way is clear
Wait — green is next, but you must not move yet
The lights have failed; treat it as a crossroads

question.explanation: The order never changes: red, red and amber, green, amber, red. Red and amber still means stop — wait for green.

steps.title: Amber on its own
steps.body: Amber alone means stop at the stop line. Carry on only if you've already crossed it, or you're so close that stopping could cause a collision.

question.prompt: The light turns amber while you're still well back. What should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line
Speed up to clear the junction before red
Carry on — amber only warns that the light is changing

question.explanation: Amber on its own means stop. You carry on only if you've already crossed the line or stopping would be unsafe.

steps.title: Green isn't automatic
steps.body: Green means you may go on only if the way is clear. If your exit road is blocked, hold back behind the line — even on green.

question.prompt: The light is green but traffic beyond the junction is at a standstill. You…

options.text: Move into the junction and wait there
Wait behind the line until your exit is clear
Go — a green light gives you right of way

question.explanation: Look into the road you're taking before you move off. Entering a junction you can't clear blocks everyone else.

steps.scene: You're in the left-hand lane at lights, waiting to turn left. Red is showing, with a green arrow pointing left.

options.text: Go straight on — a green arrow counts as a green light
Wait: an arrow never applies to your lane
Turn left if the way is clear

question.explanation: A green filter arrow lets you go in that direction only. The red still holds every other movement at the line.

a.label: Steady red
a.body: At a junction: stop behind the line and wait for the lights to change.

b.label: Twin flashing red
b.body: At a level crossing, lifting bridge or airfield: stop, and don't cross while they flash.

question.prompt: Two red lights flashing alternately mean…

options.text: Stop, and wait until they stop flashing
Cross if you can't see a train coming
Slow down and give way to traffic on the crossing

question.explanation: Flashing red means stop whether or not the way looks clear — a second train or a closing bridge may follow.

steps.title: Signals above your lane
steps.body: Overhead gantry signals apply lane by lane. A red X above your lane closes that lane — move into an open one as soon as it's safe.

question.prompt: The gantry shows a red X above your lane only. What does it mean?

options.text: Every lane ahead is closed — leave at the next exit
Your lane is closed — move into an open lane
Slow to 40 mph but stay in your lane

question.explanation: Gantry signals are lane-specific. A red X over your lane means that lane is closed — move out early, before you reach it.

steps.wrongBelief: A speed shown on a motorway gantry is a minimum you're expected to keep up to.

options.text: It's a temporary maximum for the road ahead
It's right — gantry speeds set a minimum
It applies only to the left-hand lane

question.explanation: Gantry and matrix signals show a temporary maximum for the conditions ahead. Shown in a red ring it's the legal limit.

steps.repairNote: A gantry speed is a temporary maximum, never a minimum — shown in a red ring it's the legal limit for that stretch.
